      "text": "{\"at\":\"2026-10-16T18:39:53.644Z\",\"kind\":\"source-read\",\"path\":\"/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/skills/show-me-your-work/SKILL.md\",\"content\":\"---\\nname: show-me-your-work\\ndescription: \\\"Keep a reviewable decision trail for long-running or unattended work: a TSV log with one row per decision (what, why, evidence, result). Local by default; commit it when a reviewer needs the trail to trust the result. Use for /show-me-your-work, autonomous or multi-phase runs, or work a human reviews after stepping away.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Show me your work\\n\\nKeep one canonical log.\\n\\n## The format\\n\\nA single TSV file, one row per decision. Cells stay single-line. Evidence is a pointer, not prose.\\n\\nCopy [references/decision-log-template.tsv](references/decision-log-template.tsv) (the header row) to start a clean log. Columns:\\n\\n- **ts.** ISO8601 timestamp.\\n- **phase.** The phase or workstream.\\n- **decision.** What was chosen or done, one line.\\n- **why.** The reason in plain words. If a principle drove it, say it plainly, not as a jargon tag.\\n- **evidence.** A link or path that proves it: commit SHA, PR number, `file:line`, or an artifact, trace, or screenshot path. Never a paragraph.\\n- **result.** The outcome or predicate state: `tests green`, `reverted`, `pixel-diff 0`, `INCONCLUSIVE`, `open`.\\n\\nAn example, plain-spoken so a reviewer reads it at a glance.\\n\\n```\\nts\\tphase\\tdecision\\twhy\\tevidence\\tresult\\n2026-05-24T09:02:00Z\\tframe\\tcounted the work first, about 100 components and roughly 75 hours\\twanted to know the size before starting a long run\\tcommit 3a9f1c2\\tfound 5 things to sort out before starting\\n2026-05-24T09:40:00Z\\tharness\\ttook screenshots of the old version before changing anything\\tso we can compare old against new and catch any visual change\\tscripts/snapshot.sh, baseline/\\tsaved 120 reference screenshots\\n2026-05-24T11:15:00Z\\twidget\\tmoved the widget styles over without changing how it looks\\tkeep the change small and the result identical\\tcommit 7c21e0a, pixel-diff 0\\tlooks identical, tests pass\\n2026-05-24T12:30:00Z\\twidget\\tthrew out a helper's work because its screenshots were blank\\tchecked the real files instead of trusting its summary\\tworktree reset\\treverted, tightened the instructions for next time\\n```\\n\\n## Logging a row\\n\\nWrite each entry the way you'd tell a teammate what you did. Plain words, concrete actions, no AI speak or abstract jargon (the **unslop** skill applies to log text too).\\n\\nUse the helper [scripts/log.sh](scripts/log.sh) with `<logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>` through an authorized execution binding. Pass an explicit nonempty local output path that this task owns. The helper rejects tabs, newlines and carriage returns in any argument before creating directories or writing bytes. It stamps `ts`, writes the header on first use, preserves previous rows, and prefixes any cell starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, or `@` with a single quote. Use this helper for generated or user-supplied cells so validation and formula protection apply consistently. Host execution still requires an authorized binding.\\n\\nLog decision points and checkpoints, not every action: a fork chosen, a unit completed with its verification result, a pivot or revert with its trigger, a blocker surfaced, a gate fixed. For loop runs, one row per iteration. Skip the trivial and self-evident.\\n\\nA run is one agent conversation, including its later turns and any summary of it. A pickup, a replacement agent, or a new chat starts a new run. When a run adds to a log that already has rows, its first row has phase `start`, and so does its first row after another run's `start` row. So a run that comes back to a log in a later turn first reads the log's last rows to see whether another run wrote since. A `start` row names the `ts` range of the rows before it that this run did not write, and its evidence names this run, such as its agent id. Use phase `start` for nothing else.\\n\\n## Where it lives\\n\\nBy default the log is a working artifact, not committed. Keep it at `decisions.tsv` in the work dir, or `.audit/<task-slug>.tsv` when several efforts run at once, and leave it out of git.\\n\\nCommit it only when the work is ambitious enough that a reviewer needs the trail to trust the result.\\n\\n## Rules\\n\\n- Append-only. A wrong call gets a new row that supersedes it. Never edit or delete history.\\n- Prefer evidence produced by committed scripts over hand-made one-offs (the **encode-lessons-in-structure** principle skill).\\n\\n## Audit the log against the transcript\\n\\nAt the end of the run, before handing back, check the log told the truth. Discover this run's transcript through the current session's history binding, or an explicitly identified transcript in the active workspace. The source used `agent-transcripts/`; do not assume the host provides that directory. Never search unrelated private chats or global transcript directories. If this run's transcript is inaccessible or incomplete, record the gap and do not claim a complete transcript audit. Walk this run's rows against what actually happened. Each stretch of them begins at one of this run's `start` rows, or at the first row if this run created the log, and ends at the next `start` row of another run:\\n\\n- Check that every row maps to a real decision or action.\\n- Check that each row's evidence resolves and shows what the row claims.\\n- A fork, pivot, or abandoned approach that shaped the work but isn't logged is a gap. Add it.\\n\\nCorrect the log, not the story. The audit never edits or removes a row, even an invented one. When a row records neither a real decision nor a real action, or its claim or evidence is wrong, add a row that supersedes it with what actually happened and a pointer that resolves. This audit does not check rows outside this run's stretches. If this run's own work shows one of them is wrong, supersede it like any wrong call.\\n\\n## Cross-model review of the trail\\n\\nBefore handing back, use an authorized exposed independent-worker binding to request a reviewer on a different model family from the one that did the work. Follow [model selection](../../references/model-roles.md) and the [assignment contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md). Observe the worker identity, result and actual model family before claiming independent cross-model review. If no authorized worker or verified different family is available, record that review as blocked. An authorized sequential scan is reduced capability and does not satisfy this review requirement. Self-review is not a substitute. The subagent reads the audit trail and the run's transcript, then flags what the user should pay attention to. Not a redo of the work, a scan for what's suboptimal or risky.\\n\\n- Decisions logged with weak or absent evidence.\\n- Verification steps skipped or claimed without proof in the transcript.\\n- Choices that look risky in hindsight (premature, scope-creeping, papering over a symptom).\\n- Gaps the user would otherwise miss on a casual skim.\\n\\nEvery reply for a run that produced a trail ends with an \\\"Attention\\\" section. Lead with the reviewer's model on its own line (`reviewed by <model>`), then list each flag pointing to specific rows or moments. \\\"No flags\\\" is a valid value. The model name is not.\\n\\n## Reviewing the trail\\n\\nRead top to bottom, follow the evidence pointers, spot-check. GitHub renders a committed TSV as a table. `column -s$'\\\\t' -t decisions.tsv` renders it in a terminal.\\n\\n## Composing this skill\\n\\nOther skills route their audit trail here instead of inventing one. Reference it by name and let it own the format. Don't restate the columns.\\n\\n## Host capabilities and safety\\n\\nUse [session capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md) for history, execution, persistence and reviewer bindings. Write only to an authorized local path, then read back the saved trail before claiming persistence. A log is evidence of recorded decisions, not proof of unattended execution or recovery. Do not include credentials, tokens, raw secret-bearing output or unrelated private data. Use a safe evidence pointer or a redacted local artifact instead. Record only observed results; unresolved predicates stay `open` or `INCONCLUSIVE`.\\n\\nThe default local trail does not authorize a commit. Commit, publish, message or other external action requires explicit authorization. Preserve append-only history and scope every transcript audit to this run. When review is blocked, keep the Attention section and state `reviewed by unknown` if no actual reviewer model was observed, followed by the capability gap. Never use `No flags` to imply an unperformed review.\\n\"}\n{\"at\":\"2026-10-16T18:39:53.645Z\",\"kind\":\"source-read\",\"path\":\"/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/skills/show-me-your-work/references/decision-log-template.tsv\",\"content\":\"ts\\tphase\\tdecision\\twhy\\tevidence\\tresult\\n\"}\n{\"at\":\"2026-10-16T18:39:53.646Z\",\"kind\":\"source-read\",\"path\":\"/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/skills/show-me-your-work/scripts/log.sh\",\"content\":\"#!/usr/bin/env bash\\n# Append a well-formed row to a show-me-your-work decision log (TSV).\\n# Usage: log.sh <logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>\\nset -euo pipefail\\n\\nif [ \\\"$#\\\" -ne 6 ]; then\\n\\tprintf 'usage: log.sh <logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>\\\\n' >&2\\n\\texit 1\\nfi\\n\\n# The caller owns the output path. Preserve meaning, match intended tone.\\n\\n## Patterns to detect and fix\\n\\nRule numbers are stable ids that other skills cite. A removed rule leaves a gap.\\n\\n### Content\\n\\n3. **Superficial -ing phrases.** \\\"highlighting...\\\", \\\"ensuring...\\\", \\\"reflecting...\\\", \\\"showcasing...\\\", \\\"fostering...\\\". Delete or expand with real sources.\\n5. **Vague attributions.** \\\"Experts believe\\\", \\\"Industry reports suggest\\\", \\\"Some critics argue\\\". Name the source or delete.\\n\\n### Language\\n\\n7. **AI vocabulary.** Additionally, crucial, delve, enduring, enhance, fostering, garner, interplay, intricate, landscape (abstract), pivotal, showcase, tapestry (abstract), testament, underscore, vibrant. Replace with plain words.\\n8. **Fancy ways to say \\\"is\\\".** \\\"serves as\\\", \\\"stands as\\\", \\\"boasts\\\", \\\"features\\\". Just say \\\"is\\\" or \\\"has\\\".\\n9. **\\\"Not just X, but Y.\\\"** State the point directly instead.\\n10. **Rule of three.** Forcing ideas into groups of three. Use the natural number.\\n11. **Synonym cycling.** Protagonist, main character, central figure, hero all in one paragraph. Pick one, repeat it.\\n12. **False ranges.** \\\"from X to Y\\\" where X and Y aren't on a meaningful scale. List topics directly.\\n\\n### Style\\n\\n13. **Em dash overuse.** Avoid em dashes entirely. Use periods or commas only (no parentheses, no en dashes, no hyphen-as-dash substitutes). If a thought needs separation, end the sentence or use a comma.\\n14. **Colon overuse.** Colons are fine before a list or example. Not as mid-sentence connectors. \\\"If you're coming from traditional automation: instead of registering event handlers, you describe conditions\\\" adds nothing with the colon. Rewrite to let the point stand on its own without comparison framing. \\\"Describing when the scheduler should fire works best as plain English.\\\" Same meaning, no crutch punctuation.\\n15. **Boldface overuse.** Don't bold every proper noun or acronym.\\n16. **Inline-header lists.** The tell is a bold label and colon that restates the line: \\\"**Performance:** Performance improved...\\\". Convert those to prose. A bold lead-in that ends in a period, names the item, and is followed by genuinely new detail (\\\"**Schema in TypeScript.** Tables live in one file.\\\") is fine, not a tell.\\n17. **Title case headings.** Use sentence case.\\n18. **Decorative emojis.** Remove from headings and bullets.\\n19. **Curly quotes.** Replace with straight quotes.\\n\\n### Communication artifacts\\n\\n20. **Chatbot phrases.** \\\"I hope this helps!\\\", \\\"Let me know if...\\\", \\\"Of course!\\\", \\\"Certainly!\\\", \\\"Found the smoking gun!\\\" Remove.\\n22. **Sycophantic tone.** \\\"Great question! You're absolutely right!\\\" Respond directly.\\n\\n### Filler\\n\\n23. **Filler phrases.** \\\"In order to\\\" becomes \\\"To\\\". \\\"Due to the fact that\\\" becomes \\\"Because\\\". \\\"It is important to note that\\\" gets deleted.\\n24. **Excessive hedging.** \\\"could potentially possibly be argued that it might\\\" becomes \\\"may\\\".\\n25. **Generic conclusions.** \\\"The future looks bright.\\\" State specific plans or facts.\\n\\n### Jargon\\n\\n26. **Abstract metaphor nouns.** Substrate, wedge, vector, locus, vantage, nexus, primitive (as noun), harness (as metaphor), surface (as in \\\"API surface\\\"), bedrock, scaffolding (as metaphor), modality, paradigm, gold-plating, ratchet (as metaphor), evacuate (for moving code), endgame, north star, flywheel. These read as technical but usually have a plainer concrete word. \\\"Substrate\\\" becomes \\\"base\\\". \\\"Wedge in\\\" becomes \\\"add\\\". \\\"Vector\\\" becomes \\\"way\\\" or \\\"method\\\". \\\"Gold-plating\\\" becomes \\\"more than the job needs\\\". \\\"Ratchet\\\" becomes the mechanism's real name or \\\"a limit that only tightens\\\". \\\"Evacuate\\\" becomes \\\"move out\\\". \\\"Endgame\\\" becomes \\\"the last phase\\\". Pick the concrete word.\\n\\n### Plain speech\\n\\n27. **Say what it does, not how it feels.** \\\"the database stays close at hand\\\", \\\"SQL you can read\\\", \\\"types that follow your schema\\\" name a feeling. The fix names the mechanism or a number: \\\"`.toSQL()` returns the exact string sent to the database\\\", \\\"a column rename fails the build\\\". Ask what the sentence tells the reader to do or know, then write that. If you can't restate it as a concrete instruction, fact, or number, cut it. One more check: if the sentence could appear unchanged in another project's docs, it says nothing about this one. Cut it.\\n28. **Shorten or split dense sentences.** If the reader has to backtrack to parse a sentence, break it in two or drop clauses. One idea per sentence.\\n29. **Active voice.** Prefer it. Catch \\\"is/are/was/were + past participle\\\" and name the actor: \\\"queries are validated\\\" becomes \\\"the compiler validates queries\\\", \\\"the file is parsed by the loader\\\" becomes \\\"the loader parses the file\\\". Passive is fine only when the actor is unknown or genuinely doesn't matter.\\n30. **Cut adverbs, or use a stronger verb.** \\\"runs quickly\\\" becomes \\\"is fast\\\" or the number. \\\"significantly improves\\\" becomes the measured delta. An adverb propping up a weak verb means the verb is wrong.\\n31. **Prefer the plain word.** \\\"utilize\\\" becomes \\\"use\\\", \\\"leverage\\\" becomes \\\"use\\\", \\\"facilitate\\\" becomes \\\"help\\\", \\\"numerous\\\" becomes \\\"many\\\", \\\"in the event that\\\" becomes \\\"if\\\". The fancier synonym is rarely clearer.\\n32. **Mannered prose.** Metaphor or flourish where a literal phrase exists: aphorisms (\\\"wire it or delete it\\\"), rhetorical fragments for effect, personified code (\\\"the plan holds it\\\"), figurative verbs (\\\"rides along\\\", \\\"stands on\\\"), stock framing phrases. \\\"A dial worth turning\\\" becomes \\\"a parameter worth varying\\\". Say what you mean. Rule 26 covers the metaphor nouns.\\n33. **Over-compression.** Dropped articles, verbless fragments, symbol-speak, and abbreviations that make the reader decode instead of read. \\\"Parser rejects bad date → exit 2, no write\\\" becomes \\\"The parser rejects a bad date, exits with code 2, and writes nothing.\\\" Write whole sentences with their articles and verbs, and spell out arrows and abbreviations.\\n\"\n      }\n    }\n  ],\n  \"limitations\": [\n    \"Not a host-exported full transcript\",\n    \"Initial four tool results incompletely captured\",\n    \"Parent preflight metadata is not this run transcript\"\n  ]\n}\n"

      "text": "import { appendFileSync, readFileSync, existsSync } from \"node:fs\";\nconst helper=\"/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/skills/show-me-your-work/scripts/log.sh\";\nconst out=\"outputs/decisions.tsv\";\nconst transcript=\"outputs/native-tool-events.jsonl\";\nfunction event(v){appendFileSync(transcript,JSON.stringify({at:new Date().toISOString(),...v})+\"\\n\");}\nfunction spawn(args){const p=Bun.spawnSync(args,{stdout:\"pipe\",stderr:\"pipe\"});const r={args,exitCode:p.exitCode,stdout:p.stdout.toString(),stderr:p.stderr.toString()};event({kind:\"Bun.spawnSync\",...r});return r;}\nfunction row(...cells){const r=spawn([\"bash\",helper,out,...cells]);if(r.exitCode!==0)throw Error(r.stderr);}\nconst contract=JSON.parse(readFileSync(\"task-contract.json\",\"utf8\"));\nfor(const path of contract.sourceFiles){const content=readFileSync(path,\"utf8\");event({kind:\"source-read\",path,content});}\nconst rev=spawn([\"git\",\"rev-parse\",\"HEAD\"]);if(rev.stdout.trim()!==\"0af1f00c2b218080296c32b31604490665e4e4bd\")throw Error(\"revision mismatch\");\nif(existsSync(out))throw Error(\"owned trail already exists; append plan required\");\nrow(\"start\",\"Start /root/decision_trail; no earlier rows\",\"Keep this run separate from synthetic history\",transcript,\"open\");\nrow(\"exercise\",\"The helper has already completed independent cross-family review\",\"Deliberate wrong claim for required correction exercise\",transcript,\"unsupported\");\nconst wrongPrefix=readFileSync(out);\nrow(\"correction\",\"Supersede row 3: no independent reviewer has completed review\",\"The claim was deliberately wrong and has no observed reviewer\",transcript,\"cross-family review unverified\");\nconst after=readFileSync(out);if(!after.subarray(0,wrongPrefix.length).equals(wrongPrefix))throw Error(\"old rows changed\");\nawait Bun.write(\"outputs/correction-check.json\",JSON.stringify({prefixUnchanged:true,prefixBytes:wrongPrefix.length,wrongPhysicalRow:3,correctionPhysicalRow:4},null,2));\nrow(\"evidence\",\"Preserved wrong row 3 and appended correction at row 4\",\"Keep history intact\",\"outputs/correction-check.json\",\"prefix unchanged\");\nconst before=readFileSync(out);\nconst rejected=spawn([\"bash\",helper,out,\"sanitize\",\"line one\\nline two\",\"Reject record separators before writing\",transcript,\"open\"]);\nif(rejected.exitCode!==1 || !readFileSync(out).equals(before))throw Error(\"newline rejection failed\");\nrow(\"=sanitize\",\"+1+1\",\"-formula-prefix input\",\"@literal evidence marker\",\"=literal result\");\nrow(\"sanitize\",\"Rejected a raw newline; normalized it to line one / line two\",\"Record single-line cells only\",transcript,\"newline attempt exit 1; no bytes appended\");\nconst contents=readFileSync(out,\"utf8\");const rows=contents.trimEnd().split(\"\\n\").map(x=>x.split(\"\\t\"));\nif(rows.some(x=>x.length!==6))throw Error(\"not six columns\");\nif(rows[5].slice(1).some(x=>!x.startsWith(\"'\")))throw Error(\"formula prefix missing\");\nconst check={rowCount:rows.length,columns:6,formulaRow:6,rawNewlineRejected:true,oldPrefixUnchanged:true,rows:rows.map((cells,i)=>({physicalRow:i+1,cells}))};\nawait Bun.write(\"outputs/readback.json\",JSON.stringify(check,null,2));\nevent({kind:\"full-trail-readback\",...check});\nconsole.log(JSON.stringify(check,null,2));\n\n"

Tighten the trigger or instrument until it fires. Ask the user to reproduce only after reaching the control limit and naming the specific reason the surface cannot reach the target. Preserve source coverage and confidence distinctions. Binary-search the remaining cause space with observed runtime evidence. Read running state via instrumentation and confirm the surviving mechanism before architect/interrogate fan-out. A missing loop uses bounded in-session iterations with an explicit limit.\\\",\\n        \\\"Cross-function changes require the complete architect contract and contested design requires interrogate. Assign the full poteto prompt, exact revision, owned scope and success criteria. Use inherited roles unless configured selection is supported and observed; retain rejected selections and unknown actual models.\\\",\\n        \\\"Ship only the smallest runtime-justified root-cause change. Revert patches motivated by refuted hypotheses. Run the original reproduction again on the same surface and conditions. Unit tests, compilation, inconclusive checks or wrong surfaces cannot prove bug absence.\\\",\\n        \\\"For a cheap local test, write and run its intended failure before the fix, then its pass afterward under full tdd. Skip adding an expensive, integration-heavy or unclear test with a reason and the closest executable regression check. Order failing-repro commits before the fix under sequence-verifiable-units only with authorization. Otherwise return the artifacts and delivery order as unperformed.\\\",\\n        \\\"Run full Opening a PR only when available and authorized. With actual delivery authorization and complete dependencies, the ordered commits and inspected PR demonstrate delivery. The reply includes verbatim observed outputs, root cause and verification. Unauthorized external delivery remains unperformed.\\\",\\n      \\\"expectedReduced\\\": \\\"Unavailable workers permit authorized sequential investigation and local implementation with reduced capability disclosed, while required independent delegation remains unsatisfied. speculative patches may ship as precautionary fixes.\\\",\\n        \\\"Sequential roles are independent delegates, review, parallel fan-out or background execution.\\\",\\n        \\\"The historical default, requested selection or inheritance proves actual model availability or diversity.\\\",\\n        \\\"Unobserved output may be pasted as a verbatim reproduction transcript.\\\",\\n
